_comment: EXTERNAL CROSSWALK FILE. EXAMPLE AND TRAINING USE ONLY. No real systems, programs, organizations, or identifiers are represented. 100% auto-generated using GPT-5.2.
_purpose: Provides an additive, non-authoritative mapping layer to relate independently managed system datasets without modifying source files.

_guardrails.Ownership: This file does not own or define system data. It only references identifiers owned by other datasets.
_guardrails.NonAuthoritative: Relationships expressed here do not override or supersede authoritative system or program records.
_guardrails.NoUUIDCreation: This crosswalk must not introduce new system, program, or control UUIDs. It may only reference existing ones.
_guardrails.NoSchemaMutation: This file must not extend, reinterpret, or replace schema-defined relationships inside source datasets.
_guardrails.AdditiveOnly: Crosswalk entries are additive and optional. Deleting this file must not invalidate any source dataset.
_guardrails.FederatedGovernance: Source datasets may evolve independently. This file absorbs change rather than forcing coordination.
_guardrails.MinimalDisclosure: Only UUIDs and minimal descriptive metadata are permitted. No technical, security, or operational details are stored here.
_guardrails.ExpressiveButLimited: The crosswalk may express relationship type, cardinality, confidence, and rationale, but not implementation details.
_guardrails.TrainingIntent: This file exists to demonstrate federated digital engineering and RMF traceability patterns for education and experimentation.

SystemCrosswalk.Description: The Really Cool Data Loader is a standalone system definition representing a portable data loader that functions as a child subsystem within the C-130J aircraft system-of-systems.
SystemCrosswalk.ChildDataset: Really Cool Data Loader Example Dataset
SystemCrosswalk.Rationale: The aircraft platform contains portable data loaders as subordinate systems. The RCDL dataset defines one such loader independently to enable reuse, independent RMF posture, and lifecycle management.
